text.p: WestMerchant initiated coverage of Hungarian tile manufacturer Zalakeramia Rt with a "buy" rating, saying the stock was undervalued compared to its longer term earnings prospects.

"We initiate our coverage with a buy recommendation as the current valuation fails to reflect the medium to longer-term earnings prospects for what is fast becoming the leading regional ceramic manufacturer," analysts Robert Feuer and Martin Catling said in a company report, dated June 12.

The analysts expected the company's earnings to decline this year with earnings per share (EPS) falling to 422 forints from 441 forints in 1996, due to the "dilution effect of the recent equity issue and the integration costs of the newly acquired companies."

"However, we estimate a healthy real advance of over 80 percent in 1998 and are optimistic about the longer-term," Feuer and Catling said. They expect Zalakeramia's EPS to jump to 866 forints in 1998.

Zalakeramia has implemented three acquisitions this year, acquiring majority stakes in Croatia's ceramics manufacturer Inker, Hungary's tile maker Pietra and Romania's tile and sanitary ware manufacturer S.C. Cesarom S.A.
"We anticipate that shareholder value will be further enhanced by additional complementary acquisitions," the analysts said.
On Tuesday Zalakeramia shares ended at 7,555 forints, down 145.
